rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient that is very unlikely to truncate any of the 10 compounds while giving a usable spread of retention times across the run. A mid temperature should modestly shorten retention and reveal whether the key optimization lever is the gradient window, slope, or temperature.

All 10 compounds eluted early and the resolution term is already perfect, so the next step is to trim the gradient window around the observed elution region to cut time while keeping all peaks inside the gradient. This should test whether a narrower, better-focused window can preserve the separations around peaks 5–7 while improving the time term.

The narrowed window made the run slower, so the broad window was better; now test a steeper version of that successful method to reduce analysis time while checking whether the critical 5–7 region still keeps adequate resolution. This directly probes how sensitive the closest pair is to gradient slope.

The 10 min gradient is fast but over-compresses the critical cluster around peaks 5–7, while 20 min fully resolves everything; a midpoint slope should recover enough resolution there without sacrificing too much time. This is the most direct refinement around the current optimum.

The only remaining weakness is the 6/7 pair, and it improved strongly from 10 to 14 to 20 min, so a slightly shallower gradient than 14 min may push that pair to baseline resolution while keeping the run short enough to preserve an excellent CRF. This is a focused slope refinement around the current best method.

Since the 6/7 pair is only weakly resolved at the fastest near-optimal slope, the next lever is temperature, which can shift selectivity for close pairs with little time penalty. Dropping T slightly may separate that critical pair enough to beat the 14 min, 40 C method while keeping the run comfortably short.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity, so test the opposite direction at the current best slope to see whether a modest increase in T improves the critical cluster instead. Close-pair order/selectivity can shift with temperature, and 45 C should still keep the run very short.

Temperature moves away from 40 C both made the critical cluster worse, so return to 40 C and refine slope on the fast side of the optimum. A 12 min gradient will map the CRF maximum between 10 and 16 min and may still outperform 14 min if the resolution penalty remains modest.

The best CRF is near 14–16 min, and extending from 14 to 16 min already restored full resolution with only a small time penalty; 18 min will define whether the true optimum sits just beyond 16 min. This is the last key slope point needed to bracket the maximum cleanly at the proven best temperature and window.

The optimum clearly centers on 14 min at 40 C, so now test whether a slightly lower phi1 can keep all compounds in the gradient while reducing unnecessary high-organic range and improving selectivity in the crowded middle cluster. This probes the last plausible lever besides slope, without risking truncation because the last peak already elutes very early.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.85 improved CRF and still kept every peak inside the gradient, so continue trimming the high-organic end slightly to see if selectivity in the critical 6/7 region improves further without adding too much time. The current best method suggests there is still excess gradient range above the last eluting compounds.

The improvement at phi1 = 0.85 and decline at 0.80 suggest the optimum phi1 is likely bracketed between 0.85 and 0.95. Testing 0.90 will map that local maximum and may preserve full resolution with a smaller time penalty than 0.85.

The best region is now clearly phi1 = 0.90 at 40 C, and the limiting factor remains the 6/7 pair. Lengthening the gradient slightly from 14 to 16 min at this improved phi window should raise that pair above 1.5 while likely keeping the time penalty small enough to challenge the current best CRF.

At phi1 = 0.90, moving from 14 to 16 min cost too much time, so the remaining opportunity is a slightly steeper version that might still retain enough resolution while reducing run time further. This will map whether the local CRF maximum at phi1 = 0.90 is exactly at 14 min or shifted toward 12 min.

The optimum is tightly localized at phi1 = 0.90, tG = 14, T = 40, so the remaining unexplored lever is the low-organic start. Raising phi0 slightly may improve the balance of the early and crowded mid-run region without truncation, since the first peak is still well retained and far from the void.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved CRF further, so test one more step upward to see whether the optimum start composition is even closer to the actual elution window. The first peak remains safely retained, and this is the cleanest remaining local refinement around the current best method.

The best point so far is phi0 = 0.10, phi1 = 0.90, suggesting the low end is near optimal while the high end may still warrant a small check on the other side of 0.90. Testing phi1 = 0.95 with the improved phi0 will determine whether the optimum high-organic endpoint is truly centered at 0.90 or slightly higher.

With phi0 = 0.10 established as best, test the opposite side of the phi1 optimum to confirm whether 0.90 is truly the maximum or whether a slightly lower endpoint gives even better selectivity for the limiting 6/7 pair. This completes a clean local bracket around the current best composition window.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so the only sensible use of remaining budget is to map nearby equally good conditions. Combining the successful phi1 = 0.85 with the slightly improved higher phi0 trend tests whether a small upward shift in the start composition also preserves the perfect score.

We already have a perfect score, so now map the robustness plateau in the phi0 direction at the best phi1, tG, and T. Pushing phi0 one more step higher will show how far the perfect window extends before the earliest peaks get too close to unretained behavior or the critical pair begins to compress.

With a perfect score already achieved at 14 min, the most useful remaining test is robustness in gradient slope around that optimum. A slightly longer gradient at the best composition window will show whether full resolution is maintained with any time penalty and help define the flatness of the optimum.

Since longer tG around the perfect window only adds time, test the faster-side robustness for the other perfect composition point. This will show whether phi0 = 0.15, phi1 = 0.85 still stays near-optimal at a steeper slope or whether 14 min is a sharp optimum there too.

With composition and slope already mapped and multiple perfect methods found at 40 C, use one remaining run to test temperature robustness of the best method. A lower temperature could reveal whether the perfect score is narrowly tied to 40 C or whether nearby thermal conditions also preserve full performance.

Temperature robustness remains the only untested dimension around the second perfect method, and 35 C clearly hurt selectivity. Testing 45 C at the other perfect composition checks whether the optimum is specific to 40 C or whether the high side is also viable near the best window.

For the final run, map one last adjacent composition around the perfect plateau by lowering phi1 from the successful 0.85 at phi0 = 0.15. This checks the lower boundary of the optimum window and could reveal whether the perfect score extends further than currently shown.
